chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa' from Aban ibn Uthman from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala' from Abu Abdillah from his father (peace be upon them) said:

The houses of Makkah did not have doors, and the people of the cities would come with their pitch (bitumen), so they would enter and strike (the walls) with it. And the first one to install doors for it was Muawiya.
ai.seo_question: Who introduced doors to the houses of Makkah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in Al-Kafi, highlights a significant socio-architectural shift in Mecca by attributing the introduction of doors to houses to Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan, thereby marking the end of the open, communal living style characteristic of the pre-Islamic and early Islamic eras. In Shia scholarly tradition, this change is often interpreted as a move towards increased privacy and stratification, reflecting the broader political and social transformations under the Umayyads. The narration serves as a tangible historical marker for the transition from the simplicity of the Prophet's time to the more formalized domestic structures of the caliphate.
